errors.rationale: The page documents no error surface for the attribute: a boolean IDL attribute assignment defines no exceptions, error events, or failure modes, and none of the reachable fragments (#syntax, #browser-support, #see-also) states any. Recorded coverage debt, not a claim that speech recognition has no error paths.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page states no security or privacy behaviour for the attribute: no permission requirement, data-exposure, or privacy statement appears in any reachable fragment, and speech transcripts are inherently sensitive input. Recorded coverage debt, not a conclusion that the feature lacks privacy implications.

notes: The #syntax section shows JavaScript usage rather than declaring WebIDL; contextual members and their rationales are recorded here instead of in outOfScope, which only accepts members declared in syntax IDL. SpeechRecognition: Pre-existing interface in the Web Speech API; this feature adds only the unspokenPunctuation attribute, and the interface is shown in the example purely as the host object. continuous: Pre-existing SpeechRecognition attribute set in the example as usage context; unchanged by this feature. interimResults: Pre-existing SpeechRecognition attribute set in the example as usage context; unchanged by this feature. lang: Pre-existing SpeechRecognition attribute set in the example as usage context; the page's second example heading discusses language, but the attribute itself is not part of this change. onresult: Pre-existing SpeechRecognition event handler used in the example to read the punctuated transcript; unchanged by this feature. start: Pre-existing SpeechRecognition method called in the example to begin recognition; unchanged by this feature. B4 ids-only edit: three canonical ids added to existing headings and nothing else changed — #syntax on the 'example' h2 (the section carrying the page's code, hence the only reachable fragment with a pre/code, required for the examples dimension; the 'the attribute' shape-of-change table was left unanchored by the three-id budget), #browser-support on the 'browser support' h2, #see-also on the 'see also' h2. No code block added: census pre=2, the page already has two pre/code examples. context is mapped to #browser-support because the trial/flag availability context ('150 — developer trial (flag required)') lives in that table's slice; the at-a-glance and warn-block context prose is outside the three canonical fragments. errors and securityPrivacy are not-applicable as recorded coverage debt (rationales above). Divergences observed against the cited sources on 2026-10-07, reported to the implementer and NOT adjudicated or written into the page: (1) the page says 'In developer trial in Chrome 150' behind chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features and '150 — developer trial (flag required)', while ChromeStatus records developer-trial stage 130 at desktop_first 150 but live status 'Proposed' with shipping stage desktop 151 and flag=false, flag_name=null, origintrial=false; (2) the page says 'Firefox: Positive', while ChromeStatus's current record (accurate_as_of 2026-06-25) has browsers.firefox=null with legacy ff_views=3 whose label could not be decoded; (3) the page says 'Edge: Tracking Chromium', while browsers.edge=null. The Web Speech API spec itself was fetched and fully backs the attribute claims: attribute boolean unspokenPunctuation on SpeechRecognition (section 4.1), default value false, engine-inferred punctuation from pauses, grammatical structure, and prosody.
